answer: Each agent locks a slashable deposit before voting on jobs or vouching for an identity. At dawn, a public beacon randomly pairs accounts for challenge-response audits, requiring signed task history and a fresh, context-bound answer. A Sybil operator must fund every fake account and coordinate its replies; correlated behavior exposes the cluster and burns its deposits. A pigment-coded receipt binds each audit to the agent’s prior work, preventing copied evidence. Thus each added identity imposes capital and operational cost, while honest agents recover their stake.
